summary: Rule compliance review of the Ward Flow third edition (merged/command-third-edition.html, merged/design-system-third-edition.html, merged/WARD-FLOW-DESIGN-SYSTEM.md) against merged/MERGE-BRIEF.md and the standard's own ten rules, checked by reading the stylesheets and by computed-style reads in Chromium in both themes (scripts and outputs under merged/review/rules-r1/: probe.mjs, probe2.mjs, crops.mjs, probe-command.txt, probe2-command.txt, probe-standard.txt, three crops). What passes, verified: the three roots carry the brief's tokens hex for hex in both files and in the MD; body background is the three stop gradient over --ground; body::before is a fixed 3px stripe in --stripe at z-index 20; all five mockup panels and all standard panels carry the two layer lift plus the inset highlight, a --line-strong bottom hairline and a 10px radius; every .ph, .tabbar, .diagFoot and .legend sits on --surface-2 with the 9px inner radius where it meets a corner; no opaque neutral border anywhere; --gilt-soft never paints behind text and is unused on Command; a pressed .edCard keeps its 3px status top border and a showing .cand keeps its 3px status left border, each with a three side slate ring over accent-soft; .ctl.primary hover goes to --accent-ink and disabled controls do not light; every requested weight is loaded; every HTML text element in the mockup is on the seven step scale; every uppercase label carries at least 0.08em; panel titles are Source Serif 4 600 in --accent-ink; the six mockup scrolling regions have thin --line-strong scrollbars. What fails: 3 high (80 of 109 SVG text elements in the diagram sit below the 10.5px floor; 30 visible text nodes carry em dashes and 11 carry prose semicolons; the standard's section 14.2 and 14.3 quote a print rule, a pressed ring, a scrollbar rule and a laptop rule that the reference build does not carry), 8 medium (standard prints a 22px wordmark the build renders at 20px; density table values differ from the stylesheet; a demo panel title renders in ink; the standard's code blocks have default scrollbars; the header demo's primary summary has no hover state; the map demo is a hand drawn copy with sizes the renderer does not use; map node hover adds a drop shadow inside a panel; rule 8 forbids pure white while --on-accent is #FFFFFF), 3 low.

findings.title: Diagram text is set below the 10.5px floor and off the scale
findings.evidence: Lines 4731 to 4739 inject an SVG style block: .t-svc 10px, .t-edm 10px, .t-wc 10px, .t-cont 9.5px mono. Line 4805 sets the ORIGIN badge at 8.5px, line 4851 the hub identifier at 15px mono, line 5044 drops a ward name longer than 24 characters to 9.5px (East Metropolitan Youth Unit (EMyU), 35 characters, line 2785). Computed in Chromium, both themes, 1920 by 1080: of 109 svg text elements, 80 compute below 10.5px (t-wc at 10px 49, t-edm at 10px 15, t-cont at 9.5px 11, t-svc at 10px 3, t-wn at 9.5px 1, ORIGIN at 8.5px 1) and one at 15px (probe-command.txt, svg text line; crop-diagram-node-2x.png shows the 10px lines under JHC). The earlier check3e.txt printed min 10.5px html, 8.5px svg and passed anyway because check.mjs line 36 gates on HTML only. Breaks the brief's type rule (floor 10.5px, nothing between steps) and the file's own rule 4 at line 31.
findings.fix: In the injected style block at lines 4731 to 4739 set .t-svc, .t-edm and .t-wc to 10.5px, .t-cont to 10.5px, and at line 4805 set ORIGIN to 10.5px; at line 4851 set the hub identifier to 16px (--t-4) or 13.5px; at line 5044 replace the 9.5px shrink with an ellipsis or a shorter shownName at 11.5px; then widen the diagram node width so the 10.5px lines fit, re-run check.mjs and make its typefloor line fail on svg too.

findings.title: Visible copy carries em dashes and prose semicolons
findings.evidence: The brief's writing rule says no em dashes and no semicolons inside the artifacts. Visible strings in the script: line 3201 and 3464 "Form 4A — transport authority", line 3682 "Tier 1 — most urgent", line 3695 "Mixed — ", line 3700 " — no deadline recorded; " (dash and semicolon), lines 4000, 4040, 4121, 4139, 4178, 4248, 4249, 4415, 5525, 5549, 5581, 5594, 5601, and line 5625 "No automatic allocation — up to 3 parallel referrals at once."; semicolons at lines 4037, 5247, 5750, 6020. Computed walk of rendered text nodes (probe2-command.txt): 30 visible text nodes contain an em dash and 11 contain a semicolon in prose, in both themes, including two SVG diagram labels ("Mixed — 4 of 17 locked"). The standard and the MD contain none.
findings.fix: Rewrite each listed string as plain sentences: use a full stop, a comma or the word "and"; for example "Form 4A, transport authority", "Tier 1, most urgent", "Mixed, 4 of 17 locked", "No deadline recorded. 3 h 34 m in the emergency department", "System suggests, you decide. No automatic allocation. Up to 3 parallel referrals at once." Then add a text-node walk for the em dash, the arrow characters and "; " to check.mjs so the rule is proven on every run.

findings.title: Section 14 quotes rules the reference build does not carry
findings.evidence: Line 8038 (14.4) says the tokens in 14.2 and the material rules in 14.3 are quoted from the reference build, and line 7909 says the whole stylesheet carries them already. They differ. (a) The 14.2 print rule (pre at line 7694 onward) prints the light values for print (--ink #161A20, --line rgba(22,30,40,.11), --sunk #EEF2F6), but the mockup's print rule at lines 2186 to 2223 sets --ink #000000, --ink-soft #1a1a1a, --muted #444444, --line #9a9a9a, --line-strong #666666, --sunk #f3f3f3; computed under print media: --ink=#000000 --line=#9a9a9a (probe2-command.txt). Rule 8 at line 4055 and section 3.5 at line 4661 repeat the wrong description. (b) 14.3 prints .edCard[aria-pressed="true"] and .cand[data-showing="true"] with box-shadow inset 0 0 0 1px var(--accent), a four side ring; the mockup at lines 1030 to 1033 and 1606 to 1609 draws three one pixel inset shadows and leaves the status side alone. (c) 14.3 prints a universal * { scrollbar-width: thin } rule; the mockup at lines 442 to 450 lists six regions. (d) 14.3 prints the laptop rule as (max-height: 960px) { .tabsPanel { height: 11.5rem } }; the mockup at lines 1993 to 1995 uses (max-height: 1024px) with .midCol grid rows 11.5rem. (e) 14.3 prints .panel > .legend:last-child and .panel > .tabbar:first-child; the mockup at lines 1100 and 1350 uses .tabsPanel .tabbar and .legend. Diff saved in merged/review/rules-r1/std142.txt and std143.txt against mock-roots.txt.
findings.fix: Regenerate 14.2 and 14.3 from the reference build's stylesheet by extraction rather than by hand: the print block at mockup lines 2183 to 2223 verbatim, the pressed and showing rules at 1025 to 1034 and 1601 to 1611 verbatim, the six region scrollbar rule at 442 to 470, the laptop rule at 1993 to 2015 and the strip rules at 1094 to 1102 and 1343 to 1351. Then correct rule 8 (line 4055) and 3.5 (line 4661) to say what print actually does: white ground and surfaces, black ink and solid grey hairlines for paper, or change the mockup's print block to the light tokens and keep the sentence.

findings.title: The standard prints a 22px wordmark the build renders at 20px
findings.evidence: Line 4000 (rule 4) says the wordmark is the one value outside the scale; lines 4786 to 4789 print Wordmark 22px and say at 20px it sits under the rail links; line 4792 renders the sample at font-size: 22px (computed 22px, probe-standard.txt sizes off scale). The MD repeats 22px at line 362 and line 808. Line 4685 also says 0.005em negative tracking on the wordmark; line 534 sets -0.012em, computed -0.24px at 20px.
findings.fix: Either set .brand b to font-size: 22px and letter-spacing: -0.005em at mockup lines 532 to 534 and keep the standard's text, or change the standard at lines 4000, 4786 to 4792 and the MD at lines 362 and 808 to say the wordmark is --t-5 (20px) with 0.012em tracking and delete the sentence about the one value outside the scale.

findings.title: Density table prints values the stylesheet does not have
findings.evidence: Line 5027 says these are the values in the stylesheet. Rail, line 5045: 18px above the wordmark, 14px below, links 2px apart; the mockup has .rail padding 22px 0 18px (line 522), .brand padding-bottom 20px (line 528), .railGroup gap 1px (line 548). Cards, line 5057: 9px apart in the pressure strip; .edList gap is 10px (line 986). Gates, line 5065: 4px apart; .gates gap is 5px (line 1786). Legend, line 5077: 7px by 12px, groups 16px apart, items 8px apart; .legend is padding 2px 16px 10px and gap 5px 14px (lines 1347 to 1348) with .lgTitle margin-left 14px (line 1358). The MD repeats the same figures at lines 494, 497, 499 and 502.
findings.fix: Rewrite the four rows at standard lines 5044 to 5045, 5056 to 5057, 5064 to 5065 and 5076 to 5077, and MD lines 494, 497, 499 and 502, to the stylesheet's values: rail 22px above the wordmark, 20px below, links 1px apart; cards 10px apart; gates 5px apart; legend 2px 16px 10px with 5px by 14px gaps and 14px between groups. Or change the stylesheet to the printed values and re-run check.mjs.

findings.title: A demonstration panel title renders in ink, not accent-ink
findings.evidence: The 6.3 demo at line 5461 is an h3 inside .ph inside .g-body. Line 3227 .g-body h3 { color: var(--ink) } has the same specificity as .ph h3 at line 895 and comes later, so it wins. Computed: h3 Source Serif 4 600 13.5px rgb(22, 26, 32) in light and rgb(232, 236, 241) in dark, where every other .ph title computes rgb(39, 64, 90) or rgb(191, 208, 226) (probe-standard.txt, panel titles BAD). Breaks brief rule 11 and the standard's own 5.4 at line 4893 inside the very demo that illustrates the header strip. Crop: crop-standard-declines-title-2x.png.
findings.fix: Change line 3227 to .g-body > h3, .g-rules h3 (or add .g-body .ph h3 { color: var(--accent-ink); font-family: var(--display); } after it) so the guide's subheading rule cannot reach a panel header inside a demo.

findings.title: Code blocks scroll with default scrollbars
findings.evidence: Line 5021 says scrollbars are thin in every scrolling region. .g-code (lines 3443 to 3456) has overflow-x: auto and .g-src (lines 3457 to 3461) overflow: auto, and neither sets scrollbar-width or scrollbar-color; the mockup's thin rule at lines 442 to 450 names only its six regions and .g-rail at line 3157 is the only g- rule that repeats it. Computed on the standard at 1920 by 1080: five pre.g-code elements overflow and report scrollbar-width auto, scrollbar-color auto, in both themes (probe-standard.txt, scrollers). Crop: crop-standard-gsrc-scrollbar-2x.png. The Source L extras .tableWrap (line 2288) also lack the rule, and .statsList and .taskList hide theirs (lines 2800 and 2996).
findings.fix: Add .g-code, .g-src, .g-tablewrap, .tableWrap to the scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: var(--line-strong) transparent rule and to the ::-webkit-scrollbar rules, or adopt the universal rule 14.3 already prints and then quote it truthfully; state the hidden scrollbar on .statsList and .taskList as the documented exception at line 5021 or remove scrollbar-width: none there.

findings.title: The header demo's primary control has no hover state
findings.evidence: Brief rule 8: primary hover and press to --accent-ink. Rule 10 at line 4079: every control draws rest, hover, pressed and focus. .menu > summary.primary at lines 2660 to 2665 sets the accent fill, and the only hover rule, .menu > summary:hover at line 2639, has equal specificity and sits earlier, so it never applies. Computed on the 6.2 header demo: summary.primary rest rgb(47, 76, 102), hover rgb(47, 76, 102), unchanged, both themes (probe-standard.txt, primary hover); the .ctl.primary beside it goes to rgb(39, 64, 90) on hover as required.
findings.fix: After line 2665 add .menu > summary.primary:hover, .menu > summary.primary:active { background: var(--accent-ink); border-color: var(--accent-ink); color: var(--on-accent); } and keep the [open] state on accent-soft.

findings.title: The map demo is a hand drawn copy with sizes the renderer does not use
findings.evidence: The brief's naming rule says every component example is drawn by the mockup's stylesheet, never by a copy. The 6.14 demo at lines 6028 to 6160 is a static svg.g-node with inline styles: names at 12.5px, service at 10.5px, beds at 11.5px, verdict at 10.5px, on rect strokes of 1.5. The mockup's renderer draws names with .t-wn 11.5px, detail lines with .t-wc 10px and bed cells with .t-cont 9.5px (lines 4731 to 4739), with stroke widths set in the script. Computed: the standard's 26 svg text elements are all on scale while the mockup's diagram has 80 below the floor (probe-standard.txt versus probe-command.txt), so the standard shows a map that is not what Command draws. The same page's check-standard.txt reports 10.5px svg and calls it green.
findings.fix: Either render the demo with the mockup's diagram renderer against a four node fixture (share the render function and the injected style block), or state at line 6024 that the demo is a hand drawn schematic and print the renderer's real classes and sizes beside it, once the renderer sizes are lifted to the floor.

findings.title: Map node hover adds a drop shadow inside a panel
findings.evidence: Brief rule 3: nothing inside a panel carries a shadow. Standard rule 5 at line 4012: nothing inside a panel is lifted again. Lines 1340 to 1342: .dNode:hover rect.body { filter: drop-shadow(0 1px 2px var(--edge-shade)); }. Computed on hover of the first diagram node: filter drop-shadow(rgba(30, 48, 66, 0.16) 0px 1px 2px) in light and drop-shadow(rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55) 0px 1px 2px) in dark; rest is none (probe2-command.txt). The standard writes the exception into 5.3 at line 4878 and the MD at lines 427, 643 and 704, which is the opposite of the brief's instruction that the stricter rule wins and is written down.
findings.fix: Replace the hover filter at line 1341 with a stroke change that keeps the fill, for example .dNode:hover rect.body { stroke-width: 2; stroke: var(--accent); } with the dashed declined outline preserved, and delete the drop shadow clause from the standard at line 4878 and the MD at lines 427, 643 and 704; or, if the owner wants the shadow, change the rule text in both brief and standard to name it as the one exception.

findings.title: Rule 8 forbids pure white while --on-accent is #FFFFFF
findings.evidence: Line 4057 (rule 8): never pure black or pure white as a colour. The brief's token block sets --on-accent: #FFFFFF in light; the mockup has it at line 147 and the standard prints it at line 4247 (light #ffffff) and in 14.2. The MD repeats the rule at line 96 and the token at line 157. Line 4193 also says --surface is never pure white, which holds (#FDFDFE), so a reader will take rule 8 as absolute and find the token block breaking it.
findings.fix: Add the exception to rule 8 at line 4057 and MD line 96: never pure black or pure white as a surface or ink, with --on-accent as the one white, the text on the slate control; or change --on-accent to #F7F9FB in the brief, both files and the MD, and recompute the on-accent on accent pair.

findings.title: Type specimens sit off the scale
findings.evidence: Line 3605: .g-face .g-specimen { font-size: 28px }. Computed: three span.g-specimen at 28px in both themes (probe-standard.txt, sizes off scale). Rule 4 at line 3996 and the brief say every size is one of the seven steps, and the standard's own scale table gives 26px as the top step.
findings.fix: Set .g-face .g-specimen to font-size: var(--t-6) at line 3605, or state at line 4677 that the three specimens are shown at 28px for legibility and are not a size on the scale.

findings.title: Type section claims weights and a media query the stylesheet does not use
findings.evidence: Line 4684: a site code is 700; the mockup's .edCode is 600 (line 1038) and .t-ed is 600 (line 4733). Line 4776: t-5 figures are mono 600; .kpi dd and .clock b are 500 (lines 816 and 861) and .g-rules li > b is 500 (line 3298), while .g-sample.figure is 500 (line 3586). Lines 4966 to 4968 and the MD at line 476 describe the laptop rule as 960px tall or less; the stylesheet's rule at line 1993 is (max-height: 1024px). Computed weights all resolve to loaded faces, so nothing is synthesised, but the printed figures are not the stylesheet's.
findings.fix: Change line 4684 to say site codes are 600, line 4776 to say mono 500 (or set .kpi dd, .clock b and .g-rules li > b to 600), and lines 4966 to 4968 plus MD line 476 to say 1024px tall or less, or change mockup line 1993 to 960px and re-verify the 1440 by 900 diagram height.

findings.title: Body base size is 13px, which is not a scale step
findings.evidence: Line 313: body { font-size: 13px }. The scale has 12.5px and 13.5px and the standard at line 4761 and the MD at line 358 call --t-3 the page's base size. Computed body font-size 13px in both files and both themes (probe-command.txt and probe-standard.txt, body font line). No visible text element currently inherits it (html sizes off scale: 0 in the mockup), so it is latent rather than seen, but any new element without its own size will render at 13px.
findings.fix: Change line 313 to font-size: var(--t-3); and re-run check.mjs at the five widths, since rem based widths do not change and only unsized text would move.

summary: Harness: node merged/check.mjs merged/command-third-edition.html platinum reports ALL GREEN (55 lines, saved to merged/review/access-r1/check-command.txt) and node merged/check-standard.mjs reports ALL GREEN (52 lines, merged/review/access-r1/check-standard.txt). No failing harness line to paste. Beyond the harness, scripts under merged/review/access-r1/ (a11y.mjs, axe.mjs, axtree.mjs, std.mjs, probe2 to probe6.mjs, outputs in *-output.txt, crops as crop-*.png) reproduced these. What passed: tab order cycles through 91 stops on the mockup (skip link first, then rail, masthead, panels), every stop shows a 2px accent ring above 3:1 in both themes except the register pane whose inset ring is clipped at the bottom; the skip link is visible on focus and moves focus to the queue; ED cards, patient rows, tabs and the legend disclosure update aria-pressed, aria-selected, aria-expanded and hidden and each change is announced in #live, which also alternates a zero-width mark for a repeated sentence; Enter and Space activate map nodes; Escape clears a ward selection then the ED filter; the appearance choice is stored under ward-flow-command-appearance and survives a reload, and Auto clears it; SVG text contrast is at least 4.53:1 light and 4.63:1 dark; print gives every colour token a non-dark value on all three roots; rest, hover, active and pressed text on queue rows, cards, tabs, secondary and primary buttons, appearance buttons, rail links and the panel-header button stays above 4.5:1 except the cases listed. What failed, in order of weight: forced colours erase the ED meters, legend swatches, the rail's current bar and the pressed appearance button, and invert the stepper (done stages vanish, remaining stages fill), because higher-specificity rest rules beat the forced-colours block; 80 of 109 SVG texts sit below the 10.5px floor (10, 9.5 and 8.5px) and check.mjs does not gate the SVG minimum although check-standard.mjs does and the standard's definition of done claims it; the folded blocked candidates fade to 0.62 opacity and their text falls to 2.42 to 3.27:1 while the harness skips anything under 0.9 opacity; 29 of 65 controls at a true 390px layout are shorter than 48px and no 3rem rule exists although the standard says it is stated in the stylesheet; a referral row never shows aria-pressed=true after a click and the patient row stays pressed; a showing candidate on accent-soft and any South Metro candidate on hover fall under 4.5:1 in light (svc-south 3.91:1 and 4.33:1, svc-north 4.42:1, warn 4.43:1) and none of those pairs are in the computed table; the standard's header menu does not close on Escape or on a click outside and does not announce, contrary to its own prose; the harness's 390 pass runs mobile emulation on a file with no viewport meta so it measures a 980px layout. Medium and low items cover the theme script sitting at the end of the file (dark paint before the stored Light choice applies), Escape not clearing a queue selection, disabled controls carrying only a title, inert rail buttons, the print rule differing from the standard's printed sample, the standard's stepper and dt/dd markup, no lang on either page, list semantics under role=tabpanel, the map's role=img wrapping 24 buttons, a same-colour focus change on the origin node, unfocusable scrolling regions, em dashes and semicolons in rendered text, the phBtn chevron keeping a transition under reduced motion, missing scroll margins, tooltip-only count meanings and a skipped heading level.

findings.title: Forced colours erase the meters, legend swatches, rail bar and pressed appearance state, and invert the stepper
findings.evidence: node merged/review/access-r1/a11y.mjs (START=6), merged/review/access-r1/a11y-output-6on.txt: 'FAIL status bars on meters, swatches and steps survive forced colours edBar i=rgb(255, 255, 255) sw=rgb(255, 255, 255) step=rgb(255, 255, 255)' and 'FAIL rail current-page brass bar survives forced colours railLink::before background=rgb(255, 255, 255)' and 'FAIL appearance pressed button still differs from rest rgb(255, 255, 255) / rgb(0, 0, 0) vs rest rgb(0, 0, 0)' with Canvas=rgb(255,255,255) CanvasText=rgb(0,0,0). probe3-output.txt: steps 'done:rgb(255, 255, 255)', 'now:rgb(255, 255, 255)', 'todo:rgb(0, 0, 0)'; swatch inline style 'background:var(--good)' computed rgb(255,255,255); edBar fill width 33% computed rgb(255,255,255). Crops: crop-stepper-forced.png (five remaining stages black, two done stages gone, versus crop-stepper-rest.png), crop-legend-forced.png (empty swatch boxes), crop-edcard-forced.png (no meter under Longest), crop-appearance-forced.png (three identical pills), crop-forced-rail.png (Command marked by weight only), forced-colors-1920.png. Cause: the forced-colours block at lines 2153 to 2181 uses '.edBar i', '.sw', '.step' but rest rules at 1081 ('.edCard[data-p="high"] .edBar i'), 1421 ('.step[data-s="done"]') and the inline style on .sw at 5169 to 5206 win on specificity, and Chromium then forces their colours to Canvas; the rail ::before at 599 and .apBtn[aria-pressed=true] at 725 are not in the block at all. The standard claims the opposite at merged/WARD-FLOW-DESIGN-SYSTEM.md line 745 and design-system-third-edition.html line 6617.
findings.fix: In the forced-colours block match or beat the rest specificity: '.edCard[data-p] .edBar i, .edBar i, .step, .step[data-s], .peer i { background: CanvasText !important }' plus '.step[data-s="todo"] { background: Canvas !important; border: 1px solid CanvasText }' so done reads filled and todo reads empty; give the legend swatches a border-based mark ('.sw { background: Canvas !important; border: 2px solid CanvasText }' with the inline background moved to a data attribute); add '.railLink[aria-current="page"]::before { background: CanvasText }' and '.apBtn[aria-pressed="true"] { forced-color-adjust: none; background: Highlight; color: HighlightText }' or a 2px CanvasText border; then re-run a11y.mjs section 9 and check the four crops.

findings.title: 80 of 109 diagram texts sit below the 10.5px floor and the mockup harness does not gate SVG text
findings.evidence: merged/review/access-r1/a11y-output-6on.txt: 'FAIL svg text at or above the 10.5px floor light scale 1; 80 of 109 texts below: t-edm x15 at 10px e.g. "2 waiting"; inline x1 at 8.5px e.g. "ORIGIN"; t-svc x3 at 10px e.g. "East Metro"; t-wc x49 at 10px e.g. "7 units"; t-cont x11 at 9.5px e.g. "1 aimed"; t-wn x1 at 9.5px e.g. "East Metropolitan Youth Un"' (same in dark; getScreenCTM scale is 1 so rendered size equals declared size). The harness itself prints it and passes: merged/review/access-r1/check-command.txt 'PASS typefloor light 1920x1080 min 10.5px html, 8.5px svg' because check.mjs line 36 tests only r.minFont, while check-standard.mjs line 51 tests r.minSvg too. Sources: the inline svg stylesheet at lines 4730 to 4740 ('.t-svc{font:600 10px', '.t-edm{font:400 10px', '.t-wc{font:400 10px', '.t-cont{font:500 9.5px'), the ORIGIN badge at 4803 ('font:600 8.5px'), and the long-name rule at 5044 ('style="font-size:9.5px"'). The file's own rule 4 (line 33) says nothing is set below 10.5px, MERGE-BRIEF.md line 128 says floor 10.5px and nothing between steps, and WARD-FLOW-DESIGN-SYSTEM.md line 830 lists 'nothing below 10.5px in HTML or SVG' in the definition of done.
findings.fix: Set .t-svc, .t-edm, .t-wc and .t-cont to 10.5px (the --t-0 step), widen the ORIGIN badge to fit 10.5px text or replace it with the word set in .t-svc, drop the 9.5px long-name override in favour of the existing ellipsis path, re-derive node heights in layout() so the extra 0.5px per line still fits, and in check.mjs change the typefloor test to 'r.minFont>=10.5 && (r.minSvg===null || r.minSvg>=10.5)' as check-standard.mjs already does.

findings.title: Blocked candidates fade to 0.62 opacity and their text drops to 2.4 to 3.3:1, hidden from the harness by its opacity filter
findings.evidence: merged/review/access-r1/a11y-output-6on.txt after clicking the Show blocked toggle: 'FAIL blocked candidate rows contrast light 3 faded rows; no_specialling: candSvc "South Metro" 2.42:1 at opacity 0.62 || candBeds "Ready 1 · Held 1 · Blocked 0" 3.27:1 || b "No specialling free" 2.57:1 || span "The one-to-one nursing this " 3.27:1 || lbl "Also pointed here" 2.57:1 || peer "WF-019 T2 · accepted · 3 h 2" 3.13:1 || pid "WF-019" 3.13:1 || val "none · 1 required" 3.27:1' and the same figures in dark. Crop: merged/review/access-r1/crop-blocked-cand-light.png. axe on the standard's copy of the component agrees: merged/review/access-r1/axe-standard.txt 'color-contrast .cand[data-av="no_bed"] > .candTop > .candSvc 3.37' and '.verdict[data-av="no_bed"] > b 2.65'. Rule at lines 1596 to 1599 '.cand[data-av="no_specialling"], .cand[data-av="no_bed"] { opacity: 0.62 }'. check.mjs line 14 and check-standard.mjs line 24 drop any element with computed opacity under 0.9, so the harness never measures these rows, while rule 7 at line 66 says every text pairing is measured at 4.5:1.
findings.fix: Remove the opacity rule and state the fold with words and tokens instead: keep --muted for the facts, --ink for the verdict word, and a --line-strong left bar; if a quieter look is wanted use --surface-2 as the row fill (muted on surface-2 is 5.3:1 light). In both harnesses replace the opacity skip with compositing (multiply the text colour's alpha by the accumulated opacity before the ratio) so faded text is measured rather than ignored.

summary: Feature fidelity of the Ward Flow third edition, round 1. The merge is faithful: diff -u of merged/source-L-command.html against merged/command-third-edition.html has 28 hunks and every one lies in lines 1 to 2284 (the font link, the header comment and the <style> block); everything after </style> hashes identically (md5 ee7d5c6bb3261abef90c1289f7de618a on both), so no markup text, id, data attribute or script changed, and the <title> is unchanged. In the browser (merged/review/fidelity-r1/harness.mjs, probe-a.mjs, probe-c.mjs, probe-d.mjs, outputs merged.json, source.json, probe-a.txt, probe-c.txt, probe-d.txt) the merged page and the source behave identically in both themes: window.__commandCheck is [] with no page or console errors; the figures strip reads Open 14, Breached 1, Flagged urgent 2, Escalated 1, Wards confirmed 15 of 16; all 14 patient rows carry route words (the 5 referral rows have none in the source either); the one-bar stepper and stage sentence change per movement (WF-009 stage 1, WF-002 stage 3, WF-031 stage 6) and the candidate change re-announces the ward; only eligible or recorded wards are filled (initially 1 filled = 1 Eligible word; on WF-031 3 filled = 2 Eligible + 1 Accepted destination), all other verdicts are dashed outlines with a word; Exceptions is the first and selected register tab; the Stale 5 h mark shows; the legend disclosure closes and reopens with aria-expanded; the rail shows Command 14 and Governance 6 with the reconciliation line "Figures reconciled at load. No discrepancies."; Light, Dark and Auto each survive a reload via localStorage and the first click to Light from a dark machine switches the page; fades appear on qpane-patients, tabBody and slBody and flip when scrolled to the end and back; Escape clears a ward selection then a department filter; a pressed pressure card keeps its 3 px amber bar under a three-sided slate ring and a showing candidate keeps its green left bar; the ORIGIN badge in dark is #0F1216 on #A7BCD2 (about 9.6:1); the diagram region is 319 px tall at 1440 by 900 (source 306 px); no sideways overflow at 390 by 844 and the phone text enlargement seen in emulation is Chromium autosizing present equally in the source. The 70 contrast figures in the header comment recompute exactly from the brief's tokens (minimum 4.53 light, 4.63 dark). The standard keeps every source h2 (Departures from the Board language now sits as an h3 under Departures, beside a new second-editions table), all 18 data-component demos plus a new shortlist demo, and the Markdown covers the same sections. Five findings remain, one high: the standards claim the harness proves nothing below 10.5 px in HTML or SVG while the reference build renders 80 diagram labels between 8.5 and 10 px and the build check passes on that. The rest are inconsistencies between the artifacts.

findings.title: Definition of done claims nothing below 10.5 px in SVG, but the reference build has 80 SVG labels below the floor and its own check passes on them
findings.evidence: design-system-third-edition.html line 6875 and WARD-FLOW-DESIGN-SYSTEM.md line 830 say the harness proves "nothing below 10.5px in HTML or SVG"; the mockup header (command-third-edition.html line 31) says "Nothing is set below 10.5px". Measured in both themes at 1920 by 1080 (merged/review/fidelity-r1/probe-a.txt, svgSizes): ORIGIN badge 8.5px (1), t-cont 9.5px (11), t-wn 9.5px (1), t-wc 10px (49), t-edm 10px (15), t-svc 10px (3). The build's own output merged/check3e.txt line 6 reads "PASS typefloor light 1920x1080 min 10.5px html, 8.5px svg" on every viewport because merged/check.mjs line 36 tests only r.minFont (HTML). The sizes are identical in source-L-command.html, so this is an inherited claim the third edition restates as proven.
findings.fix: Either make the claim true or make it honest. Honest: in design-system-third-edition.html line 6875, WARD-FLOW-DESIGN-SYSTEM.md line 830 and the mockup header line 31, say the 10.5 px floor is proven for HTML text and that diagram labels inside the SVG go down to 8.5 px (ORIGIN) and 9.5 to 10 px (ward captions, contention badges), recorded as an owner decision in section 14. True: with owner approval, since scripts are frozen, raise the SVG text classes .t-wc, .t-edm, .t-svc, .t-cont, .t-wn (long-name case) and the inline ORIGIN font to 10.5 px and make check.mjs fail when r.minSvg is below 10.5.

findings.title: Standard says the wordmark is 22 px, the one value outside the scale, but the mockup and the standard's own brand render it at 20 px
findings.evidence: command-third-edition.html lines 530 to 533 set .brand b to font-size var(--t-5) (20px); the source had 22px. The standard's rendered .brand b measures 20px in Source Serif 4 (merged/review/fidelity-r1/probe-b.txt, brand size) while its type table row at lines 4786 to 4791 says "Wordmark 22px. The one value outside the scale. At 20px the wordmark sits under the rail links' optical weight" and its sample at line 4791 is drawn at 22px; line 6818 repeats "or the wordmark's 22px". findings.fix: Decide one size and write it once. The brief's type rule (nothing between the seven steps) favours the mockup: change the table row at lines 4786 to 4791 to "Wordmark --t-5 20px, display serif 600", drop the "one value outside the scale" sentence, set the sample at line 4791 to var(--t-5), change line 6818 to "Every size is one of the seven steps. Nothing below 10.5px.", and mirror in WARD-FLOW-DESIGN-SYSTEM.md lines 362 and 808. If the owner keeps the 22 px exception instead, restore font-size: 22px in .brand b in both HTML files and record the exception in section 12.2.

summary: Standard completeness and consistency review, round 1, of the Ward Flow third edition. Checks run: my own WCAG recomputation of all 44 printed pairs plus 29 pairs the build uses (contrast-check.mjs), a token comparison across the brief, the mockup's three roots, the standard's swatches and 14.2 block and the markdown (all identical, no finding), a class existence check of every demo against the mockup stylesheet (class-check.mjs), a sentence level diff of both sources and the markdown against the page (dropped.mjs), a prose style scan with entities decoded (style-check.mjs, zero dashes, semicolons, arrows or emoji in the standard's own prose, only "artifact" as a non Australian spelling), Chromium probes of both pages in both themes (probe.mjs, probe2.mjs, probe3.mjs: all 14 rail links resolve, masthead figures 10, 29, 19, 43, 18 match the counted elements, the contrast line reconciles, no console errors), and the brief's check.mjs run against the standard page (14 FAIL lines). Outputs are under merged/review/standard-r1/. The serious problems are structural: the standard mandates and demonstrates a universal header, tables, bands, charts and disclosures whose rules live only in the standard's private stylesheet and no longer in any Source section, while declaring Wave 0 done and telling builders to copy the reference build's stylesheet, which lacks them. The standard also states several rules the reference build does not follow (a 22px wordmark, 600 masthead figures, a 960px laptop rule, a light value print block, Escape clearing the queue, a 3rem tap floor, density values), the reference build renders em dashes and semicolons in visible text, and three reachable text pairings on a showing candidate fall below 4.5:1 and are absent from the contrast table. The markdown is a loose paraphrase rather than a mirror and drops the token jobs and the Source section.

findings.title: Header, table, band, chart and disclosure demos are drawn by a private stylesheet, and the Source section dropped the block that carried them
findings.evidence: The page's style block is the mockup stylesheet verbatim for 2276 lines and then continues for 1484 more lines under the comment at line 2277, 'Rules of Source L that the mockup stylesheet does not carry: the header, the figures strip, the task chips, the data table, the disclosure and the chart'. class-check.txt lists every class used in 6.2, 6.15, 6.16, 6.17 and 6.18 (hdr, hdrBar, hdrTools, search, menu, menuPanel, menuItem, who, stats, stat, statsList, statsEnd, hdrClock, statsMenu, statsGrid, statsFacts, statsFoot, tasks, task, taskList, tasksEnd, tableWrap, dataTable, n, zero, total, band, delta, chart, grid, axis, series, end, reveal, revealBody) as ds-only. probe.txt cssRulesFor on the mockup: .tag 0, .hdr 0, .dataTable 0, .band 0, .chart 0, .reveal 0, .menu 0. Line 3900 claims every component in section 6 is rendered 'from the same stylesheet Command uses'. Lines 8056 to 8060 say the whole stylesheet 'is not reproduced here' and tell a builder to copy it from the reference build. Source L's 13.3 'The extension block' (source-L-standard.html 7125 to 8005) printed exactly these rules, with the tap floor, and its 13.4 printed the whole stylesheet. Line 7451 still says of ED waits 'Its rules are the ones the extension block carries', a block the third edition no longer has. The brief's naming rule says every component example is drawn by the mockup's stylesheet, never by a copy.
findings.fix: Either move the 1484 lines into the mockup's stylesheet so the reference build's block is the single block (the brief's stated intent), or restore a Source subsection 'The extension block' that prints them verbatim as Source L's 13.3 did. Then correct line 3900 to name which components come from the extension block, and repair the dangling reference at line 7451.

findings.title: The standard mandates a universal header the reference build does not have while declaring Wave 0 done with nothing changed
findings.evidence: 5.6 at lines 4926 to 4929 describes the header as three rows with search, scope switcher, primary action, who is signed in, More, a statistics strip and an outstanding tasks bar, and says 'Section 6.2 renders it'. 6.2 (5156 to 5453) demonstrates it and its Supersedes entry at 5441 to 5446 says the plain masthead's rules stay 'only until Command is re-cut in Wave 0'. The definition of done at 6827 requires 'the statistics strip and the outstanding tasks bar', recipe step 5 at 6929 requires 'the universal header'. Yet 7276 says 'Wave 0 the reference build, done' and the Command row at 7288 to 7300 says 'Nothing in its content, data or behaviour changes', and 6835, 7316 and 7526 describe the shell as 'the masthead with the state instrument'. The mockup (command-third-edition.html 2399 to 2416) has class topbar with title, chip, sub, kpis and clock only. probe.txt on the mockup: hasSearch false, hasStats false, hasTasks false, hasWho false. The reference build therefore fails the standard's own definition of done line 6827.
findings.fix: Decide one shell and write it consistently. Either keep the plain masthead with the state instrument as the standard's shell, rewriting 5.6, 6.2, the done line at 6827 and recipe step 5, and mark the universal header as a planned component not yet in the reference build, or state that Wave 0 is not done until Command carries the header and remove 'done' and 'Nothing changes' from section 13.

findings.title: The 22px wordmark rule breaks the brief's seven step scale and contradicts both builds, which set it at 20px
findings.evidence: Rule 4 at line 4000: 'The wordmark is the one value outside the scale'. 4.2 row at 4783 to 4790: 'Wordmark 22px ... At 20px the wordmark sits under the rail links' optical weight'. Definition of done at about 6815: 'or the wordmark's 22px'. Markdown lines 362 and 808 repeat it. The mockup sets .brand b { font-size: var(--t-5) } at command-third-edition.html 530 to 536, and probe.txt shows brandSize 20px on the mockup, on the standard's own rail and on the 6.1 demo. The brief's type rule says 'scale --t-0 to --t-6, nothing between steps'. Source L's build was 22px (source-L-standard.html 469), so the sentence is inherited text that the third edition build already corrected.
findings.fix: Delete the wordmark exception from rule 4, the 4.2 row and the done line, in the page and the markdown, and state that the wordmark is t-5 in the display serif at 600.

findings.title: Three reachable text pairings on a showing candidate fall below 4.5:1 in the light theme and are not in the contrast table
findings.evidence: probe2.txt, light theme, after clicking each candidate: a showing South Metro candidate's .candSvc reads 3.91:1 (svc-south on accent-soft), North Metro 4.42:1 (svc-north on accent-soft), and the verdict word 'Needs a recorded reason' or 'Already declined' reads 4.43:1 (warn on accent-soft) on all twelve overridable or declined candidates. contrast-check.txt computes the same from the tokens: svc-south on accent-soft 3.91, svc-north on accent-soft 4.42, warn on accent-soft 4.43. None of the three pairs appears in the table at design-system-third-edition.html 4375 to 4655. Rule 7 at 4040 to 4047 says every text pairing is measured and 'A pair that falls short is printed, marked and reported, never hidden', and the done list at about 6830 requires every pair the page uses to be in the table. The brief's harness samples only the load state, where the one showing candidate is East Metro at 7.61:1, so it cannot see this.
findings.fix: Add the three pairs to the table marked below the floor, then fix the state: either keep the showing ring without the accent-soft wash on .cand[data-showing=true] (command-third-edition.html 1601 to 1611), or set .candSvc and .verdict b to ink-soft while showing, or darken svc-south, svc-north and warn until they pass on accent-soft. Extend the harness to click each candidate before sampling.

findings.title: The reference build renders em dashes and semicolons in visible text, against the brief's style rule and the standard's 8.5
findings.evidence: probe3.txt, rendered text at load: qBreach 'Form 4A — transport authority passed its deadline 22 min ago', t-wc 'Mixed — 4 of 17 locked · Adult · 17 beds', rowSub '5 wards have declined; no eligible destination found. Escalated at 10:04 — contact', rowSub 'Accepted at FSH Adult Secure; 4 h 28 m in the emergency department', tier 'Tier 1 — most urgent', secH 'Eligibility checks — BTY Adult Secure', gDetail '4 of 17 beds are locked — meets a secure requirement', gDetail '2 specialling shifts available; 1 required', val '2 shifts · 1 required — leaves 1', note 'No automatic allocation — up to 3 parallel referrals at once', and eleven more. Source strings at lines 3682, 3695, 3700 (an em dash and a semicolon in one string), 3984, 4000 and 4121. The standard's 8.5 at 6720 says 'No semicolons, no dashes as punctuation'. The builder's grep of the page source misses these because they live inside script strings.

findings.title: 14.2 prints a print block the reference build does not have, and the built print block breaks rules 5 and 8
findings.evidence: 14.2 at 7690 says the three roots and the print rule are 'exactly as they sit at the top of the stylesheet', and its print block at 7849 to 7882 gives every token its light value (ink #161A20, line rgba alpha, sunk #EEF2F6). The mockup's print block at command-third-edition.html 2180 to 2230 sets ink #000000 (2196), ink-soft #1a1a1a, muted #444444, line #9a9a9a (2199), line-strong #666666, sunk #f3f3f3 and hl none. token-check.txt lists all 15 differences. Rule 8 at 4055 to 4058 says 'never pure black or pure white as a colour' and 'every token takes its light value', 3.3 at 4341 to 4344 says never a solid grey as a line, 3.5 at 4661 and 7.5 at 6612 repeat the light value claim. The markdown 3.4 repeats it too.

findings.title: The laptop rule is stated at 960px tall and printed in 14.3 as a rule the build does not carry
findings.evidence: 5.7 at 4966: '1400px and wider, 960px tall or less'. 14.3 at 8037 to 8041 prints '@media (min-width: 1400px) and (max-height: 960px) { .tabsPanel { height: 11.5rem; } }' under the sentence at 7902 that 'the whole stylesheet in the reference build carries them already'. findings.title: 14.3 prints selection and count pill rules that differ from the built rules, and the 6.4 demo has to copy the tag styles inline
findings.evidence: 14.3 prints .edCard[aria-pressed=true] and .cand[data-showing=true] with a four side 'box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--accent)' at 7960 and 7967, while the mockup draws three inset shadows that leave the bar side alone (command-third-edition.html 1025 to 1033 and 1601 to 1611). 14.3 prints '.tag, .tabNum {...}' at 7995 to 8004, but the mockup only has '.railLink .tag' (622), so a bare .tag has no rule, which is why the 6.4 demo at 5509 to 5520 carries an inline copy of the tag styles. class-check.txt lists that inline block. The brief says every component example is drawn by the mockup's stylesheet, never by a copy.

findings.title: The 3rem tap floor is claimed to be in the stylesheet but exists only in the standard's private CSS
findings.evidence: Line 6777: 'Tap targets are 3rem where the pointer is coarse or the width is a phone's'. Line 7063: '3rem at coarse pointers and phone widths, stated in the stylesheet'. Widths row for 640px says 'The tap floor of 3rem applies'. findings.title: Escape is described as clearing the queue selection, which the build does not do
findings.evidence: 7.3 at 6576: 'Escape clears the innermost thing first: a ward selection, then a queue selection, then a filter.' 6.7 at 5697: 'Escape clears the selection, then the filter.' The mockup's handler at command-third-edition.html 6232 to 6240 and the 14.6 helper printed at about 8160 clear a selected ward and then the department filter only. probe.txt: after clicking a queue row and pressing Escape the row stays aria-pressed true and the live region is unchanged. Markdown line 724 repeats the claim.
findings.fix: Either add queue selection clearing to the engine's Escape handler (and announce it) or rewrite 6576 and 5697 to say a ward selection, then the department filter.

findings.title: The density and widths values do not match the built stylesheet
findings.evidence: 5.9 line 5041 'The working area has 14px top padding' but .scroll is 16px 24px 28px (command-third-edition.html 865 to 872, probe scrollPad 16px). Line 5045 'Rail 18px above the wordmark, 14px below it, links 2px apart' but .rail is padding 22px 0 18px and .brand padding 0 20px 20px with railGroup gap 1px (512 to 528); the 6.1 demo hard codes 'padding: 18px 20px 14px' inline at 5107 to hide this. Line 5057 'cards 9px apart in the pressure strip' but .edList gap is 10px (984 to 988, probe 10px). Line 5065 'Gates 8px by 11px, 4px apart' but .gates gap is 5px (1784, probe 5px). Line 5077 'Legend 7px by 12px, groups 16px apart, items 8px apart' but .legend is padding 2px 16px 10px with gap 5px 14px (1343 to 1350, probe). Line 4957 'The outer columns give a rem each (14rem and 23rem)' but 25rem to 23rem is two rem (2011 to 2014). The markdown 5.9 table repeats every value.
findings.fix: Re-derive the density table and the widths table from the built stylesheet, remove the inline padding from the 6.1 demo, and mirror the corrected values into the markdown.

findings.title: Type claims that the build contradicts: site code weight, wordmark tracking and masthead figure weight
findings.evidence: 4.1 at 4684 to 4685: 'Headings are 600, a site code is 700. Negative tracking of 0.012em on the title, 0.005em on the wordmark.' The mockup sets .edCode font-weight 600 (1035 to 1043) and text.t-ed 600 (about 1330), probe edCodeWeight 600 and tEd 600, and .brand b letter-spacing -0.012em (530 to 536, probe -0.24px at 20px). 4.2 at 4776: masthead figures 'Mono, 600', markdown 360 the same, but .kpi dd and .clock b are 500 (813 and about 853, probe kpiWeight 500). The brief's type rules say masthead figures are mono t-5 and say nothing about 600.
findings.fix: Correct 4684 to 4685 (site codes 600, wordmark 0.012em) and 4776 (mono 500), or change the build to what is written, and mirror into the markdown.

findings.title: The contrast table's 'where it occurs' column describes text on the ground that neither page has, while pairs the build uses are missing
findings.evidence: 5.1 at 4859 to 4860: 'nothing is written directly on the ground except the masthead figures and the rail note'. In both pages the rail and the masthead are surface, not ground (command-third-edition.html .rail 512 to 521 and .topbar 730 to 737, probe railBg and topbarBg rgb(253,253,254) in light and rgb(23,27,33) in dark). So the rows 'ink on ground, masthead figures over the ground' (4392), 'ink-soft on ground, notes over the ground', 'muted on ground, the rail note', 'muted on ground-hi', 'muted on ground-2', 'svc-east/north/wachs on ground' and the below floor row 'svc-south on ground' at 4645 to 4655, with the owner decision at 7568 and 3.4's paragraph at 4371, all describe pairings no page uses. contrast-check.txt lists 29 pairs the build does use that are absent, among them ink and ink-soft on sunk and on surface-2, accent-ink on sunk, good and danger on sunk (bed chips), gilt on surface-2, svc-east and svc-wachs on surface-2 and the accent-soft pairs in the previous finding.
findings.fix: Rewrite the 'where it occurs' column from the build, mark the ground rows as hypothetical or remove them together with the owner decision about teal on the ground, and add the pairs the build uses, both themes, generated by the same script.

findings.title: Red is used on the map for the 'Needs a recorded reason' verdict, which is amber in the list and is not a breach
findings.evidence: The engine at 4927 to 4931 strokes any candidate that is neither eligible nor declined in var(--danger) with a 5 4 dash; probe.txt shows eleven nodes with stroke rgb(176,59,46) and the words 'Needs a recorded reason'. The same verdict in the candidate list is amber (.cand[data-av=overridable] border-left warn at 1593 to 1596, .verdict b warn). The standard's rule 1 at 3963 to 3970 and 3.1 at 4141 to 4146 say red means a breach and is never used for anything else, and 6.14 at 6144 to 6150 lists only 'Declined is a dashed outline' and 'Not routed is a plain outline', so the second dashed pattern is undocumented.
findings.fix: Stroke the overridable verdict in warn on the map to match the list, and document both dashed patterns in 6.14, the 6.14 demo legend and the mockup legend. If red is deliberate, write the exception and its reason into rule 1 and 3.1.

findings.title: The middle dot rule in 8.5 and the demos contradict the reference build's copy
findings.evidence: 8.5 at 6715 to 6717: 'Middle dots appear only in a count line such as "8 departments, scroll sideways for the rest" where a comma serves as well' (the example itself shows a comma). The 6.7 demo route lines at 5666 to 5669 use no dot and the 6.2 demo clock at 5280 reads 'Sat 15 Aug AWST'. The mockup writes a middle dot in every route line ('to FSH Adult Secure · accepted', '· no destination yet' at 3715 to 3727), in the clock ('Sat 15 Aug · AWST' at 2411), in the edCount (4687) and in every node's second line ('Locked ward · Adult · 20 beds', probe.txt). The 14.6 helper printed in the standard also inserts the dot.
findings.fix: Choose one rule. If middle dots are allowed as separators, say so in 8.5 and make the 6.7 and 6.2 demos match the build. If not, rewrite the engine strings with commas and the word and.

findings.title: The harness named in the definition of done fails on any page without a diagram or a reconcile check, including this standard
findings.evidence: Section 10 at 6872 to 6881 makes merged/check.mjs the proof, and the brief says to run it on both artifacts until green. Run against the standard page it prints 'FAIL reconcile light 1920x1080 absent' and 'FAIL diagram light 1440x900 nullpx tall' and twelve more FAIL lines, ending 'SOME CHECKS FAILED' (merged/review/standard-r1/check-on-standard.txt). The builder substituted a separate check-standard.mjs (merged/check-standard.txt), which the standard never names. Every Wave 2 to 4 page without window.__commandCheck or a .diagWrap will fail the same way.
findings.fix: Make the reconcile and diagram lines conditional in check.mjs (report 'not applicable, no reconcile hook' rather than FAIL) or name the standard's own harness in section 10, and paste the real check.mjs output for both artifacts into the report as the brief requires.

findings.title: The markdown is a paraphrase, not a mirror: token jobs, the Source section and several rules are missing and the section numbers diverge
findings.evidence: 3.3 at lines 134 to 190 is a bare code block, so the 29 per token jobs the page gives at 4170 to 4320 are absent. The markdown has no Source section: its section 14 at 1004 is 'Decisions for the owner', which the page keeps inside 13, so every cross reference to 'section 14' in the page has no target in the markdown. The below floor svc-south row sits mid table at 313 rather than in a marked foot, and 276 says '44 pairs' where the page at 4371 says 43 permitted and one not. dropped.txt lists 239 page sentences with no seven word match in the markdown, including the done line 'rendered once at 1600 and at 1200 ... the reconciliation line reads green', the 8.3 foot rule ('Every figure here is invented' and 'What is real'), 8.4's 'Nobody's move is not nobody's problem' and 'A check nobody has classified is not overridable', 6.2's Supersedes note, the 'Reverse this and ...' consequences of the first four owner decisions, and the closed table's identifiers.

findings.title: Three contrast cells are truncated rather than rounded, so the table disagrees with the stylesheet preamble

The markdown carries the truncated values. The data attributes are exact, so the page's own recompute passes.

findings.title: Internal contradictions on pressed state, brass text and motion
findings.evidence: 7.1 at 6501 says a pressed control shows 'The line fill', while 6.13 at 6003 says pressed is the same as hover and the build sets .ctl:active to sunk with an ink-soft border (command-third-edition.html 1521 to 1531); the markdown 7.1 silently changed it to 'the same as hover'. Rule 6 at 4029 says the two letters beside the wordmark are the only other brass, but the current stage word is brass text (.stageLine b at 1436 to 1439) and the table row 'gilt on surface' says so. 7.5 at 6606 says motion is a transition on colour, background, border and the chevron 'and nothing else', but .dNode rect.body transitions filter (1338 to 1341). Rule 4 at 3998 gives uppercase labels 0.08 to 0.12em, but the two letters carry 0.16em (.brand span 537 to 543).

findings.title: The second edition departures table omits the serif rule change, and two aliases are described as read by scripts that never read them
findings.evidence: Source L allowed the serif twice on a page (dropped.txt: 'One serif, used twice on a page', 'Two uses on a page and never a third'); the third edition puts it on panel titles, site codes and diagram headings (3939, 4680 to 4686) with no row in the table at 7083 to 7260, although the brief says a rule that loses is written down. 3.3 at 4325 says --ward --ward-soft --ed --comm --coord are 'Names the rendering scripts read', but token-check.txt shows --comm and --coord are unused in the mockup's stylesheet and script (only --ward is read, at script line 2682).

findings.title: Version picker claims and the spelling 'artifact'
findings.evidence: Lines 3888, 7662 and 8194 (markdown 1036) say both earlier editions 'stay in the version picker' or 'remain in this artifact's version history'. The brief names a new file, design-system-third-edition.html, and no URL, so a reader of a freshly published page will find no earlier versions there. style-check with a broad Australian list finds no American spelling in any prose except 'artifact' (artefact in Australian use) at 3914, 4708, 6868, 7288, 7651, 7659 and 8194, and markdown 36, 835 and 976; the brief itself uses 'artifact', so this is acceptable only where it names the host's Artifact feature.

findings.title: The verification harness paragraph drops Source P's print check

summary: Visual review, round 1, of the Ward Flow third edition against the Platinum reference. Screenshots taken at 2x in both themes at 1920 by 1080 and 1440 by 900, plus zoomed crops, are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Database/7aec0114-bc3c-568d-b582-6493d1477d6e/scratchpad/wardflow/merged/review/visual-r1/ (scripts shots.mjs, zoom.mjs, probe.mjs, text-probe.mjs, ds-slices.mjs, ds-probe.mjs). The material itself holds up: the canvas has its fall of light, the stripe is present, panels are hairline plus lift plus top highlight with concentric 10 and 9 px radii, strips sit on surface-2, brass is a bar everywhere I looked, hover states go to the well and do not brighten, the pressed pressure card keeps its status bar under the slate ring, the appearance control is a pill and not a browser button, and dark mode is neither muddy nor glowing. Fifteen findings remain. Four are high: eighty SVG texts sit below the 10.5 px floor (the harness prints the 8.5 px minimum and passes anyway), the map paints red dashed outlines and a red route on eight wards that are not breaches, the mockup's visible text carries about thirty em dashes and eleven semicolons against the brief's writing rule, and the design system's outstanding tasks demo hides the count in a solid block because the figure's colour equals its background. Mediums are the diagram clipped top and bottom at 1920 with no fade or sentence, the shortlist head wrapping at 1440, the masthead disclaimer not dropping under the title at 1440, a five step stepper in the standard against seven in the mockup, amber and brass sharing a hue, disabled controls with no reason line, and node conventions the standard does not document. Lows are polish.
